evidence: gpt-oss uses `masks[u] |= 1 << v` and `masks[v] |= 1 << u`; qwen canonicalizes endpoints with `if u > v: u, v = v, u` and stores both adjacencies; glm likewise swaps endpoints and uses symmetric adjacency sets
affordance_in_statement: The records contain "bilateral non-compete agreements, each between a specific pair of suppliers" and "Two suppliers sharing such an agreement cannot be placed in the same oversight tier."
removal_suggestion: Define each input pair u v as a directed agreement from u to v, and require the directed arcs a->b, b->c, and a->c. Keep the same two-integer input format, output format, bounds, tie-break rule, and example values.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Stores every relation symmetrically as a bitset and searches common neighbors in label order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement describes agreements as bilateral relationships between an unordered pair.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Sorts each edge endpoint pair and builds symmetric adjacency sets, then searches common neighbors.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement says suppliers share an agreement rather than assigning a direction to the input pair.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Normalizes endpoints and enumerates pairs of neighbors in an undirected adjacency set.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement presents every agreement as a bilateral pair.

common_affordance: All surviving models assume that every input pair is an undirected edge and explicitly add or normalize both directions.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It performs a cubic-style enumeration over a, b, and c, causing TLE on large instances despite using adjacency sets.

recommended_edit: Change the mutable relationship semantics from bilateral agreements to directed agreements: interpret each input pair u v as u->v and require a->b, b->c, and a->c. This invalidates the symmetric-adjacency shortcut used by every survivor.
